findings.where: Article specimen: the body paragraphs, the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?', the three-item numbered list and the closing paragraph, at both widths (worst on the phone)
findings.fault: The article's running text is centred. Every line starts at a different point, so the eye has to hunt for the start of each line in long paragraphs. The numbered list is centred too, so each number sits far from its own item and the wrapped lines no longer line up under the text (item 2's text starts well to the right of item 1's). The title and byline above are left-aligned, so the page changes alignment partway through the article.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader working through one of Mark's articles, the page's 'Read' job. Centred paragraphs and lists are tiring and read as a greeting card, not a legal essay. Angélique would also object, because every article she adds would inherit this.

findings.where: Section labels below the fold: 'PALETTE' (tracked blue capitals), 'Type pair', 'An article page' and 'Motion sketch' (small bold sans), and 'Texture' (large italic serif)
findings.fault: Five labels that do the same job are set three ways. 'PALETTE' also uses the tracked capitals the page's own type note rules out ('Sentence case, never tracked capitals'), in the link blue on text that isn't a link. 'Texture' is a large italic serif heading, while its peers are small sans labels.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the tile as a type system. Labels for like sections that don't match make the hierarchy look accidental, and the blue tracked capitals break the tile's stated rules (blue only where something can be clicked; no tracked capitals). That weakens trust in the system Angélique is meant to keep up.

findings.where: Display and serif lines: 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' (blue band), 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (article title) and 'Mark's voice…' (Newsreader specimen)
findings.fault: Straight typewriter apostrophes (') appear in the largest serif lines, while the article body uses proper curly quotes (“ ” ‘ ’). At display size the straight mark stands out as a careless detail.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader and the founder. On a site selling a lawyer's precision, typewriter marks in the biggest type look careless, and they don't match the curly quotes in the body text just below.

findings.where: Article specimen: the byline 'Mark M. Moseley · Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024' under the title
findings.fault: The byline sits almost against the title's descenders, with much more space below it before the first paragraph. That reads as cramped and pairs the byline with the wrong block.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning the article head. The byline looks crammed under the title rather than set as its own line, which undercuts the calm, measured feel the tile is aiming for.
